messages:
sara: FYI customer 'acme-inc' just opened an escalation — p99 jumped ~8x starting ~14:09 UTC, users seeing slow responses and occasional 500s. customer says it started after a burst of long-chat requests. sample request_id: r-962f3a. logs attached below.

ashwin: thanks, pulling traces now. can you paste the runtime pod and tenant id? also any recent route/model rollouts?

sara: tenant: acct-acme-prod, pod: runtime-gpu-12. No deliberate rollouts from customer side. They said traffic spiked because of a campaign. snippet from runtime.log around the time:
```
2026-03-10T14:08:59Z INFO request r-962f3a route=text-gen model=redwood-13b client=acme-inc seq_len=512
2026-03-10T14:09:03Z WARN runtime memory_pressure slab_util=0.88 kv_cache=1.3GB allocator_free=24MB
2026-03-10T14:09:03Z ERROR runtime OOM when allocating 64MB: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
2026-03-10T14:09:04Z ERROR request r-962f3a status=500 p99=3.4s
2026-03-10T14:09:05Z INFO evicting KV pages count=128 reclaimed=48MB
```

maria: looks like KV cache growth + slab saturation -> allocator starved. this pattern matches previous "hotspot" cases where long sequences + many concurrent chats cause KV growth and fragmentation. can you run the small heatmap query: `/support heatmap acct-acme-prod 2026-03-10T14:00 2026-03-10T14:30` and paste results?

sara: ran it, here's summary (toplines): concurrent sessions peaked 170, avg seq_len 420, KV cache high-water 1.38GB, slab free dropped to 18MB at 14:09. p95 rose from 220ms -> 1.1s, p99 to 3.8s.

ashwin: thanks. immediate mitigation options: 1) enable active fallback routing to a smaller model (redwood-6b) for this tenant for the next 15m, 2) trigger aggressive KV eviction policy on that pod, 3) bump allocator background compaction to faster cadence. we should try (2) + (1) together.

kevin: noted — I can push a targeted policy: `rbac route-update acct-acme-prod -> model=redwood-6b ; ttl=15m` and issue `runtimectl evict-kv --tenant acct-acme-prod --force`. any concerns?

maria: evict-kv force is fine as short term; eviction will cause some tail latency for in-flight state but reduces OOM risk. also recommend enabling allocator defrag: `allocator tune --pod runtime-gpu-12 --compact-interval 30s --allow-shrink true` for 5m window. watch for CPU spike.

ashwin: quick repro checklist for postmortem: - capture per-tenant KV growth heatmap - collect allocator histograms (malloc/free sizes) - GPU memory slab fragmentation snapshot (pre/post eviction) - full request traces for the top 1% slow requests. Can someone capture `nvprof`-style or internal mem snapshots?

sara: I've asked customer to accept a short fallback to 6b. they approved. applying route update now.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline started by kevin on branch `support/evict-acme-1729502468` — job #482 queued.

kevin: eviction command run and route switch applied. monitoring.

maria: kicked allocator compaction on runtime-gpu-12. compaction log:
```
2026-03-10T14:10:12Z INFO allocator compact start slab_before=156MB slab_after=92MB reclaimed=64MB
2026-03-10T14:10:14Z INFO allocator compact done cpu_ms=218 free_after=312MB
```

ashwin: early signals look good — p95 back to ~300ms within 60s of eviction, p99 down to ~1.2s. KV cache dropped to ~420MB. keep an eye for recurring bursts.

sara: customer confirms reduced errors and faster responses. they asked what caused it so we can prevent recurrence.

maria: likely root cause = combination of long-sequence chats (high per-request KV), sudden concurrency spike causing net KV growth, plus allocator fragmentation preventing quick reclamation -> temporary OOMs and expensive evictions. Mitigations for engineering: - add tenant-level active KV soft-limits + auto-fallback when KV exceeds threshold - expose per-tenant KV watermarks to support UI - improve allocator background compaction heuristics (triggered by slab_util > 0.75) - consider adaptive KV sharding to bound per-tenant resident KV.

ashwin: action items assigned: kevin to add tenant route fallback quick-playbook + one-click from support console (P0 mitigation) — due EOW. maria to prototype allocator trigger rule (slab_util threshold) and measure CPU/latency trade-offs (start of next sprint). eng-runtime to add dashboards for per-tenant KV watermarks and a synthetic test that simulates many long-chats concurrently. I'll own the postmortem writeup.

kevin: added short runbook in support playbooks: `support/evict-and-fallback.md` with commands we ran. linking in ticket.

sara: closing loop with customer, will attach the runbook and postmortem once available. thanks team :thumbsup:
_meta: generated for dataset: slack threads about GPU memory pressure and OOM-related slowdowns; messages are realistic Slack-style and kept concise per agents.md
